result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers use a diverging percent-of-plan bar chart sorted from furthest ahead to furthest behind, with two colours separating ahead from behind and a chain-total subtitle. B labels each percentage right next to its bar and marks Northfield with a clear 'On plan' label at the zero line, while A puts its values in a separate column at the far right and draws Northfield as a small grey sliver. B's dark theme is a slight risk in email clients, but its direct labeling and gridlines make the gaps faster to read. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same core design choice: a diverging percent-vs-plan bar chart sorted from best to worst, with a blue/warm color split and actual-vs-plan dollar figures on the right. A labels each percentage right at the end of its bar and marks Northfield with a clear 'On plan' label at the zero line. B puts the percentages in a far-right column away from the bars and draws Northfield as a tiny gray sliver, though its light theme suits email better than A's dark card. B also explains clearly why it uses percent rather than dollars.
